title: Self-management of patients with tracheostomy at home - a cross-sectional study
summary:
Patients who are discharged from hospital with a tracheostomy have to learn to deal with a variety of changes. These include the care of the stoma and cannula, but also dealing with physical, social and emotional effects with possible effects on life satisfaction. The ability to deal with these changes is referred to as self-management. Self-management can be influenced by various factors.
The aim of this study is to describe the self-management of patients with tracheostomy at home. In addition, the influencing factors of life satisfaction, fears and worries as well as contacts / relationships with other people will be examined using paper-based questionnaires. 
The results of this study can help to develop measures to strengthen the self-management of patients with tracheostomy.

interventions.name: Patients with tracheostomy are interviewed once using paper-based, standardized patient-reported outcome questionnaires on self-management.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with tracheostomy who have at least one month's experience of independent or partially independent stoma care at home 
- Cognitive and motor skills as well as written willingness to participate in the survey 
- Sufficient language skills in German to read and fill out the questionnaire
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients in a palliative situation 
- Patients in long-term inpatient care
